text:
maya: quick status — after the kernel selector swap this morning I'm seeing KV cache fragmentation jump and a couple of OOMs in the p3 pool. sampling shows a lot of tiny free slots between live blocks, not usual.
liam: can you share the profiler snippet? is it prefill or decode path causing it?
maya: pasted the short output below — main signals point to prefetch/prefill allocations. decode path holds larger contiguous buffers, prefill is allocating many ~4k chunks and never coalescing.

```
# kvfrag summary (sampled)
frag_ratio: 0.18
median_free_run: 4096
oom_incidents: 3/hour
hot_requests_affecting: batch_infer_v2
```

maya: hypothesis: the kernel change increased short-lived prefetches (more micro-requests hitting the prefill hot path) and our slab allocator's free-run merging isn't aggressive enough, so we end up with high external fragmentation.
sasha: that aligns with the allocation trace I saw — many small allocations returned while larger decode buffers still pinned. Does the allocator track run age or only size bins?
jorge: allocator currently coalesces adjacent free runs only on free time, and it uses epoch-based compaction only when fragmentation > 25% (threshold in config). we didn't tune epoch frequency for the new kernel schedule.
ting: any quick mitigations to reduce immediate OOM risk while we investigate compaction strategy?
maya: short-term ideas: 1) lower prefill per-request cap to force more decode path reuse, 2) enable on-demand prefetch (deferred prefetch) for non-critical prefixes, 3) trigger background compaction more frequently during low-load windows.
liam: lowering per-request cap seems safest. what's the knob name?
jorge: `kv.prefill.max_per_request` — default 8, we can drop to 3. also `kv.compactor.scan_interval_ms` from 60000 -> 15000 for aggressive merges. note: more compaction can spike CPU.
sasha: tradeoffs: reduce cap => slightly higher tail latency for big prefills but lowers fragmentation. deferred prefetch => better memory stability but may increase token decode latency for cold prefixes.
ting: can we A/B the cap change on a small fleet subset?
maya: yes. propose: rollout plan — stage 1: set `kv.prefill.max_per_request=3` on 5% of p3 workers for 1h, collect: frag_ratio, p90 tail, OOM count. stage 2: if frag improves >10% with acceptable tail (+<5% p90), expand to 30%. stage 3: test `kv.compactor.scan_interval_ms=15000` on a different 5% group overnight.
liam: sounds good. what metrics dashboard to watch?
jorge: watch `runtime.kv.frag_ratio`, `runtime.kv.free_runs`, `runtime.oom.events`, `latency.decode.p90`, and `cpu.compactor_pct`.
maya: also add a perf counter for "small_alloc_rate" to detect the micro-chunk pressure. quick sampling command I used: `sudo /usr/bin/alloc-trace --pid $PID --small-only --out /tmp/alloc.trace`
sasha: interesting idea — also consider size-aware demotion: when a large decode buffer is live, temporarily increase prefill size bin threshold so prefill uses larger contiguous slots, avoiding small-run pollution.
ting: size-aware demotion might be a bit invasive but could be the long-term fix. can we prototype in the allocator as a conditional: if any big_buffer_count > N then prefill_bin_bias += X?
jorge: feasible. low-risk prototype: implement `allocator.prefill_bias_thresholds` and toggle via config. we can simulate with the allocator-sim harness first.
maya: immediate action items: - liam, create 5% rollout for `kv.prefill.max_per_request=3` and wire dashboards (frag_ratio, p90, oom) - jorge, spin a sim run with compactor interval 15000ms and report CPU hit - sasha, instrument small_alloc_rate and verify trace for root causes
liam: on it. will post rollout ts and quick graph in this thread :thumbsup:
jorge: sim started. initial run shows compactor CPU +5% but frag_ratio down ~12% in 3k request sim. attaching logs to the incident channel if anyone wants to dig.
oom-bot: alert: p3 pool OOM spike suppressed after 5% rollout at 1718262000, monitoring for 30m.

maya: awesome — keep thread updates small. after we validate we can design the size-aware demotion + background compaction schedule for the full rollout. also capture a short note for the release notes about the safe defaults change for `kv.prefill.max_per_request` to avoid surprises for customers.
